intro.title: Why Sustainable Cashew Farming Matters for West Africa
content: Ivory Coast is the world's largest cashew producer, but conventional farming methods often come at a cost – deforestation, water depletion, and low farmer incomes. At AfriNuts Export, we are proving that cashews can be grown differently — and we can prove it with data.

Our Farm OS doesn't just track production. It tracks our environmental footprint: water usage, organic inputs, waste diversion, and soil health metrics. This is not just sustainability — this is verifiable, tech-enabled agriculture.

challenges.title: The Problems with Conventional Cashew Farming

items.title: Deforestation & Biodiversity Loss
items.content: Cashew expansion has cleared thousands of hectares of forest in Ivory Coast, threatening wildlife and soil health.

items.title: Water Depletion & Soil Degradation
items.content: Intensive irrigation and chemical fertilizers strip soil nutrients and drain local water tables.

items.title: Chemical Overuse
items.content: Pesticides and synthetic fertilizers contaminate water sources and harm farmer health.

items.title: Waste from Processing
items.content: Cashew shells and apples are often discarded, creating waste and missing economic opportunities.

solutions.title: How AfriNuts Is Solving These Problems — With Data to Prove It

items.title: Agroforestry & Biodiversity
items.content: We intercrop cashews with native trees on our 35-hectare farm, creating habitat for local species. Every tree is mapped in Farm OS with GPS coordinates.

items.title: Water Conservation
items.content: Drip irrigation and rainwater harvesting reduce water use by up to 60%. Water metrics are logged in Farm OS for continuous improvement.

items.title: 100% Organic Methods
items.content: No synthetic pesticides or fertilizers — verified by our digital input tracking. Every application is recorded per block, per date.

items.title: Zero-Waste Processing
items.content: Cashew shells become biofuel for our processing center. Cashew apples become juice, vinegar, and animal feed. Waste diversion tracked monthly.

social.title: Social Responsibility: Our Commitment to People

farmers.title: Empowering Smallholder Farmers
content: We pay above-market prices for raw cashews from local outgrowers, eliminating middlemen so farmers keep more of their income.
We provide free training on organic farming, post-harvest handling, and business management. Our goal is to onboard 20+ local farmers into our supply chain by 2028.

labor.title: Ethical Labor Practices
content: All workers receive fair wages above the regional minimum, safe working conditions, and access to clean water on site.
We strictly prohibit child labor and conduct regular third-party audits to ensure compliance with international labor standards.

gender.title: Gender Equity in Agriculture
content: Women make up 40%+ of the agricultural workforce in Ivory Coast but often earn less and lack leadership opportunities.
At AfriNuts, we guarantee equal pay for equal work and actively recruit women for supervisory roles. Our first training cohort was 50% women.

future.title: Our 2031 Sustainability Roadmap — Tracked in Farm OS
content: By 2028: Achieve carbon-neutral status across our entire supply chain (farm to port) — progress tracked quarterly.
By 2031: Achieve zero-waste processing at our facility (shells → biofuel, apples → value-added products) — waste diversion metrics published.
By 2031: Implement blockchain traceability so buyers can track every cashew from tree to export — built on our existing Farm OS infrastructure.

endCta.title: Sustainability Backed by Technology
endCta.content: Our sustainability practices aren't just promises — they're tracked in Farm OS, verified by third-party auditors, and visible to buyers and investors. Explore how we're building a vertically integrated, ethical cashew business from farm to global markets.
